newsitem.title: USA: NY palladium storms to 17-year high, gold ranging.
newsitem.headline: NY palladium storms to 17-year high, gold ranging.

text.p: New York palladium prices stormed to a 17-year high on Wednesday as the market's nerve finally snapped on news of a strike in South Africa amid very tight physical supplies, while gold shrugged off an emerging tussle between Germany's central bank and government over revaluating reserves.
NYMEX spot June palladium settled $28.15 higher at $202.65 an ounce, just off the high of $204.00.
September, December and June 1998 contracts all settled $6.00 limit up, the maximum allowed in the forwards.
This ceiling is raised to $9.00 in Thursday's trading.
The run up in palladium and platinum, the latter back to February's highs, followed news of a wildcat strike at Amplats Rustenburg mine in South Africa, the world's biggest.
"It was the straw that broke the camel's back," a dealer said.
White metal supplies were already tight because Russia has not shipped any of its 1997 platinum and palladium exports. The cost for people to borrow the metal has soared lately.
But after close of New York trading Wednesday, Amplats said the strike was over and employees were returning to work.
NYMEX July platinum settled $13.50 firmer at $410.50 an ounce, traded $411.00 to $396.50.
Leading funds such as Tiger reportedly hold huge long positions in palladium and would make attractive sums by taking profits, dealers said.

"It would have to be the funds that sell, but they have said they are in this for the long run. They are on a roll," a producer-backed dealer said. "Why should they sell when it's going to go higher because there is no metal around."
White metals producer Stillwater Mining of North America said it benefited from Wednesday's price surge. "We will get the spot price by rolling contracts forward," spokeswoman Gina Wilson said.
NYMEX palladium stocks are just 584 ounces with open interest in June at 3,216 lots at close Tuesday with first delivery day Friday.
Meanwhile gold and silver were largely focusing on the platinum group metals, with rangebound gold trying to glean strength from them despite a huge $65 gold discount to platinum.
The yellow metal barely moved when Germany's central bank said it disagreed with government plans to revalue national reserves, a move which rattled the markets when first mooted.
Greg Drury of Mitsui USA said unless Bundesbank gold is actually sold, the market has largely discounted the revaluation plan.
Few dealers believed the Bundesbank would sell any gold, and some believed the revaluation may help to put a floor on the metal's price.
COMEX June gold settled 60 cents firmer, unable to stray from its narrow range of $345.50 to $343.10.
Bullion in late afternoon dealings was quoted at $344.60/$345.10 an ounce.
"There seems to be quite a bit of producer selling above the gold market at the $345.00 level in spot," Scott Mehlman, chief dealer at Credit Lyonnais Rouse said.

"Until we get a convincing close above $345.00, I don't think you can be too much in love with it. If we do start to see some profit-taking as a result of this temporary walkout at Rustenburg being over, then I think gold will wind its way lower," Mehlman said.
COMEX silver ended slightly lower, recovering from most of the losses suffered around the expiry of over-the-counter precious metals options at 0930 EDT.
Dealers said it was significant that July silver bounced smartly once again off the $4.65 low to end 1.8 cents down at $4.73 an ounce.
((Huw Jones, New York Commodity Desk 212-859-1646))
